 Proposed CMS Rule Would Require ACA Subsidy Checks Before Payments Begin with 2028 Plans, Not This Open Enrollment
 Published Oct 26, 2026 6:01 AM EDT 
 By
 Cole Mercer 
 Vitaly Gariev | Pexels 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services has proposed requiring Affordable Care Act marketplaces to verify key eligibility details before people receive premium subsidies . The rule was announced October 23, just over a week before open enrollment for 2027 coverage begins November 1.
 The timing may confuse, but the proposal would not change this enrollment season. CMS says the requirements would generally take effect with eligibility decisions for 2028 health plans, and only if the rule is finalized.
 For households that rely on subsidies, the bigger change would be a new yearly habit. If the rule is finalized, people who simply let their plans renew automatically could lose financial help unless they return to confirm their information each year.
 Four Checks Before Financial Help Begins
 According to the CMS fact sheet on the proposal , marketplaces would verify four things before providing advance premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions: household income and family size, citizenship or eligible immigration status, eligibility for other qualifying coverage, and place of residence.
 People could still enroll while verification is pending, but without financial assistance. They could also pick a contingent plan that takes effect only if they are later found eligible. Once eligibility is confirmed, assistance could be applied retroactively for the months they were enrolled.
 Currently enrolled consumers would be re-enrolled with subsidies only if they return each year to confirm their details and the marketplace re-verifies them. Others would be re-enrolled without financial help, which means they could face the full premium.
 The proposal implements a section of P.L. 119-21, the 2025 tax and spending law that CMS calls the Working Families Tax Cuts legislation. Because the checks apply before financial help is paid, people who buy marketplace coverage without subsidies would not face the new steps.
 A New August Window and a 30-Day Comment Period
 To give people time to gather paperwork, the rule would create a verification period starting August 1 each year. The first would open August 1, 2027, ahead of 2028 coverage.
 The proposal is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register on October 27, and the public can comment for 30 days after publication. CMS is also seeking input on stronger checks for family size and residency.
 CMS framed the change as a measure to fight fraud. "Federal subsidies should only go to eligible Americans, not to fraudsters gaming the system," CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz said in the agency's announcement .
 The agency's announcement did not estimate how many people could lose subsidies because of the new steps, and the proposal could change after public comments. That number is one of the biggest open questions, since extra paperwork can cause eligible people to drop off as well as remove ineligible ones.
 This Year's Deadlines Still Apply
 For 2027 coverage, open enrollment on HealthCare.gov runs from November 1 through January 15, according to healthinsurance.org's enrollment deadline guide . Enrolling by December 15 means coverage starts January 1. Several state-run marketplaces, including those in California, New York and New Jersey, have later end dates.
 Shoppers should expect higher sticker prices. The median proposed rate increase for 2027 individual plans is about 15%, and the enhanced federal subsidies expired at the end of 2025, healthinsurance.org reported . People who buy coverage without subsidies pay the full increase.
 Marketplaces already ask some applicants to prove what they report, and the same papers would matter more under the proposal. HealthCare.gov's document guide lists a recent tax return or W-2s if income is steady, recent pay stubs if income is changing, and a self-employment ledger for people whose income is hard to predict. Under current rules, people generally have 90 days to resolve income questions and 95 days to resolve citizenship or immigration status questions.
 Self-employed people, seasonal workers, and others whose income changes often may have a harder time documenting it. Families who move often or share housing may also need to show proof of where they live or who is in the household.
 Free, local enrollment help is available through marketplace-certified navigators. Keeping a simple folder with last year's tax return, recent pay stubs, and any marketplace letters can make both this year's enrollment and any future verification easier.
 The rule is still a proposal, and nothing changes for coverage starting January 1. MedicalDaily will report whether CMS finalizes the plan.

 Key Questions Answered
 What did CMS propose? 
 Marketplaces would verify income, family size, immigration status, other coverage, and residence before people receive ACA subsidies.
 Does this affect 2027 coverage? 
 No. The requirements would generally begin with 2028 plans and only if the rule is finalized.
 When does open enrollment for 2027 coverage run? 
 November 1 through January 15 on HealthCare.gov, with December 15 as the deadline for coverage starting January 1.
 Would automatic re-enrollment still work? 
 People would keep subsidies only if they return each year to confirm their information. Otherwise, they would be re-enrolled without financial help.
 What documents might I need? 
 Tax returns, W-2s, pay stubs, or self-employment records for income, plus documents showing citizenship or immigration status.
 Can the public comment? 
 Yes, for 30 days after the proposal is published in the Federal Register, which is scheduled for October 27.
